subject.title: feat: let plugins control inbound debounce policy

question: Should OpenClaw publish a generic `inbound_debounce` plugin SDK hook now, or keep this capability WhatsApp-owned through the scoped configuration approach in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100970?
rationale: Both open PRs address the same batching need but establish incompatible durable product boundaries: a general plugin contract versus a WhatsApp configuration surface. The repository policy requires explicit direction before expanding a shipped plugin API.

options.title: Choose the WhatsApp-owned setting
options.body: Prefer the scoped configuration design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100970 and pause this generic SDK hook until multiple channels demonstrate a shared contract need.

options.title: Sponsor the generic plugin hook
options.body: Approve this API as a cross-channel plugin contract, define its compatibility expectations, and require real WhatsApp proof before merge.

options.title: Pause both designs
options.body: Defer the behavior until maintainers establish a broader inbound-policy roadmap and a canonical owner boundary.

recommendation.title: Choose the WhatsApp-owned setting
recommendation.body: Prefer the scoped configuration design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100970 and pause this generic SDK hook until multiple channels demonstrate a shared contract need.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the repository member who acknowledged the request for direction on this exact contract.
